simplified_esrs.instrument: Commission delegated act revising the ESRS, adopted 3 July 2026
simplified_esrs.scrutiny: Two months with the European Parliament and the Council, extendable by a further two. Entry into force is expected on publication in the Official Journal, reported as 20 November 2026 — a date that depends on scrutiny concluding and is therefore not yet certain.
simplified_esrs.note: The simplified set was adopted on 3 July 2026 and cuts mandatory datapoints by 61%, moves mandatory requirements into the body of each standard, reduces the granularity of GOV-1, GOV-2 and SBM-1, relocates topical incremental requirements into ESRS 2, and replaces the minimum disclosure requirements with general disclosure requirements. The twelve-standard architecture is retained. It applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027. Reports being prepared now — FY2025 and FY2026 — are still filed under ESRS Set 1 (2023), which is the set this tool enumerates disclosure requirements against, and it says so rather than showing a preparer a DR list they cannot file against yet.
simplified_esrs.transitional: Wave-one undertakings get transitional relief: larger ones may omit certain topical standards and phase in anticipated financial effects while still reporting other material topical standards; smaller ones may omit all topical standards until financial year 2027 and report only the cross-cutting standards.
simplified_esrs.value_chain_cap: A CSRD reporter may not require a value chain company with 1,000 employees or fewer to provide more sustainability information than the voluntary standard requires. Gross Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions are carved out of that cap.

standards.name: General requirements
standards.note: Sets the architecture rather than asking for disclosures — double materiality, reporting boundary, value chain, time horizons, and how to apply the topical standards. Nothing is filed against it directly, which is why its disclosure count is zero, but every judgement in this tool is made under it.

standards.name: General disclosures
standards.note: Applies in full regardless of the materiality assessment — the one standard a preparer cannot screen out. The twelve named disclosure requirements are listed. ESRS 2 also carries the minimum disclosure requirements for policies, actions, targets and metrics (MDR-P/A/T/M), which are not separate DRs but are applied through each topical standard, so they are not counted here.

_comment: EU Taxonomy Article 8 — the disclosure every CSRD reporter owes alongside the
ESRS narrative, and the one our tool had no coverage of at all until the
competitor benchmark made the gap obvious.
Article 8 of Regulation (EU) 2020/852 requires an undertaking in scope of the
CSRD to publish the proportion of its turnover, capital expenditure and
operating expenditure associated with Taxonomy-aligned economic activities.
Three KPIs, each computed as an aligned numerator over a defined denominator,
each passed through the same four gates.
Primary sources (EUR-Lex, the Commission's sustainable finance pages) could
not be reached from the build environment, so this is drawn from law-firm and
professional-firm summaries and graded medium. Verify against Delegated
Regulation (EU) 2021/2178 as amended by (EU) 2026/73 before filing.

objectives.name: Sustainable use and protection of water and marine resources
Protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems

kpis.name: Turnover KPI
kpis.numerator: Net turnover derived from products or services associated with Taxonomy-aligned economic activities
kpis.note: The share of the business that is already green. The one investors read first, and the hardest to move in a single year.

kpis.name: CapEx KPI
kpis.numerator: Additions to tangible and intangible assets relating to Taxonomy-aligned activities, or to a credible plan to make an activity aligned
kpis.denominator: Total additions to tangible and intangible assets
kpis.note: The forward-looking one. A CapEx plan lets spend on becoming aligned count before the activity itself is aligned, which is why CapEx alignment typically runs ahead of turnover alignment in a transitioning company.

kpis.name: OpEx KPI
kpis.numerator: Direct non-capitalised costs relating to Taxonomy-aligned activities — research and development, building renovation, short-term lease, maintenance and repair
kpis.denominator: Total direct non-capitalised costs of that same defined type
kpis.note: A narrow definition, not total operating costs. Under the 2026 simplification it can be omitted entirely where it is not material to the business model, on stating the total and why.

gates.name: Taxonomy-eligible
gates.test: The activity is described in a delegated act, whether or not it meets the criteria
gates.note: Eligibility is a classification, not an achievement. Reporting high eligibility and low alignment is the normal result and is not a failure.

gates.name: Substantial contribution
gates.test: The activity meets the technical screening criteria for at least one of the six environmental objectives
gates.note: The threshold test — a numeric or qualitative criterion set per activity per objective.

gates.name: Do no significant harm
gates.test: The activity does not significantly harm any of the other five objectives
gates.note: Assessed against all remaining objectives, not only the one contributed to. The 2026 delegated act changed the DNSH criteria for pollution prevention and control.

gates.name: Minimum safeguards
gates.test: Alignment with the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, including the ILO core conventions and the International Bill of Human Rights
gates.note: An entity-level test, not an activity-level one. It fails whole KPIs rather than single activities, which is why it is assessed once and applied to everything.

simplification.note: Activities below 10% of turnover, CapEx or OpEx need not be assessed for eligibility or alignment. The test is applied to each KPI independently, so the same activity can be excluded from one KPI and assessed in another. Reporting templates were consolidated into one summary table and up to three per-activity tables. Undertakings could elect to apply the pre-amendment regulations for a financial year starting in 2025.

financial_undertakings.note: The turnover, CapEx and OpEx KPIs are treated as less relevant for financial undertakings. Credit institutions report the GAR instead. This tool covers the non-financial undertaking KPIs only and says so rather than producing a GAR it cannot defend.

checklist.name: Every reported figure traces to one stored value
checklist.why: A tagged datapoint points at a number. If the same number is retyped into the narrative, the table and the appendix, tagging surfaces the three of them disagreeing.

checklist.name: Units and scale are recorded with the figure, not in the prose around it
checklist.why: tCO2e against ktCO2e is a tagging error that reads fine to a human and fails validation.

checklist.name: Reporting period and comparatives are explicit per figure
checklist.why: The taxonomy demands a context for every fact. Figures with an implied period cannot be tagged without a preparer deciding what they meant.

checklist.name: Consolidation boundary is stated and matches the financial statements
checklist.why: A sustainability statement scoped differently from the accounts produces facts that cannot share a context with them.

checklist.name: Each disclosure is anchored to the disclosure requirement it answers
checklist.why: Tagging maps narrative to DR. A statement organised by internal chapter rather than by DR gets re-cut before it can be tagged.

checklist.name: Estimated and value-chain figures are flagged as such at source
checklist.why: The taxonomy carries the distinction. Deciding it at tagging time means deciding it after the number has already been signed off.

checklist.name: Every figure has provenance a reviewer can open
checklist.why: Not a tagging requirement. It is what makes the assurance that follows tagging survivable, and it is the part most preparers leave until last.

_comment: ESRS against IFRS S2, for the preparer doing both. This is the file that
earns its place in our tool specifically because we already run an ISSB hub:
a company reporting under IFRS S2 or AASB S2 and then pulled into CSRD should
not rebuild its climate disclosure from nothing.
Built from the joint IFRS Foundation / EFRAG Interoperability Guidance
(2 May 2024) and secondary summaries of it. The guidance PDF could not be
retrieved from the build environment, so relationships below are graded
medium and should be checked against the source table before being relied on.

sources.title: ESRS–ISSB Standards Interoperability Guidance
IFRS Foundation and EFRAG publish interoperability guidance
Joint guidance on interoperability
IFRS and EFRAG publish Interoperability Guidance on ISSB Standards and ESRS

interop.basis: A bottom-up comparison of the climate requirements of IFRS S2 against ESRS 1, ESRS 2 and ESRS E1, plus commentary on shared general principles including presentation and materiality.

mappings.note: Both ask who oversees climate and how. ESRS asks it once for all sustainability matters; a preparer writes it once and scopes it.

mappings.issb: IFRS S2 strategy — risks and opportunities
mappings.note: Material impacts, risks and opportunities against business model and strategy. The ESRS version carries impact as well as financial materiality, so the ISSB answer is a subset of it.
The process for identifying and assessing climate risk. Substantially the same disclosure.

The single strongest carry-across. Both require gross Scope 1, 2 and 3 measured under the GHG Protocol, and Scope 2 on both location and market basis. An inventory built for one is the inventory for the other.
ESRS E1 directs financial institutions to consider PCAF for Scope 3; IFRS S2 requires financed emissions disclosure for the relevant activities. Our financed emissions tool serves both.

ESRS asks for GHG reduction targets in absolute and intensity terms with base year and milestone years, and for consistency with a 1.5°C pathway. The ISSB requirement is less prescriptive about the pathway.
ESRS requires a transition plan disclosure with defined content, including locked-in emissions and alignment with the Paris Agreement. IFRS S2 asks for the plan where one exists.
Both ask for the anticipated financial effects of material climate risks and opportunities, and both allow phase-in relief in early years.
Actions and resources allocated to climate policies, with the operating and capital expenditure attached. There is no standalone ISSB disclosure requiring the spend be broken out this way.

IFRS S2 requires industry-based metrics with reference to the SASB Standards. ESRS Set 1 has no sector standards in force, so an ISSB preparer carries this across and an ESRS-only preparer does not produce it.

The structural difference. ESRS reports a topic material to the world or to the company; IFRS S2 reports what is material to the company. An ISSB assessment is never sufficient evidence for an ESRS omission.

_comment: The competitive benchmark, as data rather than as a claim in a slide.
Rules this file is held to, enforced by knowledge/build-esrs.mjs:
1. Every vendor carries at least one source URL. No coverage assertion
without one.
2. Coverage is yes | partial | no | unknown. 'unknown' is the default and
is used whenever the vendor's own material does not say. Marking a
competitor 'no' because we did not find it is how benchmarks become
marketing.
3. Our own row is graded on the same scale by the same rules, and every
'no' against us stays visible in the product.
This is a documentary review of published vendor material, not a product
trial. We have not run these platforms. Read it as 'what they say they do'.

us.name: ReGenesis Impact

honest.why: Disclosure requirements are enumerated for ESRS 2 and E1 only. The other eight topical standards stay at standard level.

The Article 8 tool computes the three KPIs from activities you enter and applies the four gates. It does not carry the technical screening criteria per activity per objective — you assert whether each gate is met, and it records that assertion. A platform that ships the criteria does something we do not.
We assess tag-readiness and state where the mandate stands. We do not tag, and are not going to. Workiva does.
The assurance pack prints provenance, data quality and its own limitations. It is not a reviewer workflow with sign-offs and role separation, which is what an audit firm actually works in.

us.note: Where we win is narrow and real: every number opens to the factor behind it with source, vintage and confidence, including the four factors we cannot source; nothing leaves the browser; and there is no sales call. Where we lose is also real and is printed above rather than left out.
